With over 300 hours researching and testing 12 of the best website builders, our in-house experts and I have shortlisted our top five recommendations for 2026. Wix is our number one choice, offering excellent website features, high-quality templates, and dependable support, making it ideal for beginners and experienced builders.

In this guide, I’ll walk you through the key features, pricing, and drawbacks of each top-rated website builder, so you can find the right fit for you.

Key Takeaways 🔍

Wix and GoDaddy have limited free plans which you can stay on forever, but you’ll need to upgrade to sell products
All of our recommendations offer AI website builders and AI tools – Wix, Squarespace, Shopify, and Hostinger have AI-powered assistants for 24/7 support

#1. Wix: Best All-in-One Builder
💰 Starting price: $17 per month (billed annually)
🤖 AI website builder: Yes
💻 Read our Wix review for more information

Wix is the best website builder I’ve tested. Wix’s extensive suite of built-in features creates a steeper learning curve for beginners compared to streamlined editors, but businesses and experienced designers will feel comfortable with what Wix offers.

✔️ Pros
Drag-and-drop editor
AI features to assist with website management
Over 2,000 free templates
24/7 help and support

❌ Cons
Can’t change template once live
Slow loading times
Limited storage space (up to 100GB, unless you choose the Business Elite plan)
Overwhelming number of features

In January, Wix launched Wix Harmony, referred to as the “company’s new flagship AI website builder.” The hybrid tool combines website building and vibe coding to help businesses develop a website from scratch. While it doesn’t replace Wix’s core website editor for now, the process lets you use natural language prompts thanks to the new AI agent, Aria, which can perform tasks for you, such as SEO. Wix Harmony is available with all Wix plans, including the free tier.

I used Wix’s AI website builder to get set up and it made the process really easy. The chatbot only asked me a few simple questions, then created a custom website and dashboard based on my responses and needs. For me, this made the building journey feel pretty conversational and collaborative. Plus, I could make any tweaks I wanted in the drag-and-drop editor afterwards. I noticed the editor ran quite slowly though, so make sure you give yourself enough time to accommodate this as you build your website.

How Much Does Wix Cost?
Wix’s pricing ranges from $17 to $159 per month (billed annually)
You can stay on Wix’s free plan forever, but it comes with a Wix domain and ads
You’ll need the $29 per month Core plan to sell online
Wix charges a processing fee of 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction

Why Use Wix in 2026?

Wix provides a user-friendly platform and built-in features to help you start, grow, and manage your website and brand online. In particular, the Wix Automations feature and AI-powered assistant, Astro, can take jobs off your hands and streamline your workflows. Not only does this save you time day-to-day, but it’s helpful for business owners who are short-staffed.

Wix is suitable for:
Users looking for a platform to both build and market their website
Users who want to get online quickly
Beginners who need a helping hand

Wix isn't suitable for:
Users who want to refresh their site’s design regularly
Users who only need the basics (Wix offers a lot of tools)

#2. Squarespace: Best for Beginners
💰 Starting price: $16 per month (billed annually)
🤖 AI website builder: Yes
💻 Read our Squarespace review for more information

According to our experts, Squarespace is the easiest website builder to use. From my testing, its beginner-friendly editor and stunning design options helped me create a modern and sleek-looking website. However, due to its grid framework, Squarespace’s editor is more restrictive than Wix’s free-form drag-and-drop interface.

Squarespace also offers great booking tools for service-based businesses, so it’s one I recommend testing if you want to offer appointments online.

✔️ Pros
Easiest drag-and-drop editor
Booking tools to offer services ( Acuity Scheduling )
Blueprint AI to build sites

❌ Cons
No autosave when editing
No free plan
Limited third-party integrations

Squarespace has introduced Pay Links to help businesses collect payments, meaning you can share a unique URL with customers via messaging apps, socials, your website, or with a QR code.

Squarespace’s Blueprint AI builder is a great starting point for anyone, especially because of its focus on brand personality. The guided experience lends a helping hand, but you’ll want to use the drag-and-drop editor to truly customize your site’s look. That said, Squarespace really handles the design work for you, which is great for beginners, but not always ideal if you want complete creative freedom. Personally, I could happily spend hours browsing Squarespace’s sections and layouts because they all look so good, especially the animated sections for new products or testimonials.

How Much Does Squarespace Cost?
Squarespace’s pricing ranges from $16 to $99 per month (billed annually)
You can test out Squarespace with its 14-day free trial
You can sell online with any Squarespace plan
Squarespace’s Basic plan charges a 2% transaction fee, but this drops to 0% from the Core plan and above

Why Use Squarespace in 2026?

In an age where AI makes us question the quality and authenticity of content, Squarespace provides a suite of comprehensive brand building tools to help you solidify your voice and identity online. From its Blueprint AI Builder for site creation to its Acuity Scheduling tool for bookings, these integrated features help you engage with customers at each touchpoint.

In fact, retaining customers through improved customer service is the number one strategy for the 322 SMBs we surveyed in January. So, Squarespace’s built-in tools will help you prioritize engagement and satisfaction.

Squarespace is suitable for:
Design-focused users and creatives
Beginners who want an intuitive builder to use
Businesses that need strong booking tools

Squarespace isn't suitable for:
Users who want to prioritize site speed (Hostinger is the fastest)
Very large online stores or businesses selling in person
Users who want phone support

#3. Hostinger: Best Budget Builder
💰 Starting price: $1.99 per month (for a 48-month subscription)
🤖 AI website builder: Yes
💻 Read our Hostinger review for more information

Hostinger is our expert recommendation for anyone with a small budget because its plans start at just $1.99 per month, which is great when SMBs are struggling with high operational costs in 2026.

Its drag-and-drop editor, suite of AI tools, and affordable starting prices make Hostinger a very beginner-friendly choice for individuals and small businesses. But, Hostinger’s cheap plans have limited features and scalability in comparison to other builders on this list, such as Wix.

✔️ Pros
Affordable starting prices
Complete suite of AI tools
Drag-and-drop editor

❌ Cons
No app market
Weak ecommerce features (sell up to 1,000 products only)
Limited scalability with two plans

Hostinger has added 100 new website templates, bringing Hostinger’s total library count to around 300. You can also filter with new category options, making it easier than ever to choose your desired template (if you don’t want to build your website with AI).

Hostinger has really been working overtime to improve its website builder and features since last year’s testing. I found the editor very intuitive and straightforward to understand, plus Hostinger’s design options are stylish and modern. This matches the backend experience too, since I could navigate my account easily! Hostinger’s streamlined approach is great for beginners and basic websites, but you’ll struggle if you need to add extra functionality due to the limitations of Hostinger’s two plans.

How Much Does Hostinger Cost?
Hostinger’s pricing ranges from $1.99 to $2.99 per month (for a 48-month term)
Get up to three months for free if you opt for a longer subscription
Renewal prices do jump up (e.g., from $1.99 to $10.99 per month)
You need the $2.99 Business Website Builder plan to sell online
Hostinger doesn’t charge transaction fees

Why Use Hostinger in 2026?

Thanks to social media and an overload of information online, consumers want to find answers, browse, and shop online with speed. To accommodate these short attention spans, Hostinger has the fastest loading times to help you engage with website visitors and potential customers right away. This is ideal in 2026, especially with the majority of website traffic coming from mobile users.

Hostinger is suitable for:
Beginners who need a simple site
Side hustlers setting up a small store
Users who need help writing website content

Hostinger isn't suitable for:
Businesses that need advanced functionality
Large ecommerce stores
Users who use third-party integrations

#4. Shopify: Best for Multichannel Selling
💰 Starting price: $29 per month (billed annually)
🤖 AI website builder: Yes
💻 Read our Shopify review for more information

If you want to sell products online, Shopify is the best ecommerce website builder on the market. It provides a dedicated platform for online stores to get started and expand, with top quality sales features that even celebrities and familiar brands rely on.

However, Shopify’s starting price of $29 per month is higher than competitors like Hostinger ($1.99 per month), making it less suitable for small-time sellers.

✔️ Pros
Sell unlimited products
Great scalability with plans
Can handle large and complex inventories
AI assistant, Shopify Sidekick

❌ Cons
Editor isn’t very user-friendly
Few free templates
Lacks advanced AI tools

It was announced in January that Shopify stores selling via ChatGPT will be charged an additional 4% fee per sale by OpenAI. This is on top of the online rates and transaction fees Shopify already charges. Increased expenses like this, as well as tariffs and taxes, are why 48% of US small businesses are planning to raise product prices in the next six months.

Shopify’s focus on inventory management and ecommerce features, such as shipping and discounts, as well as Shopify’s history of supporting large enterprises, is a reassuring sign that Shopify can work for businesses of all sizes. But, while this is all very impressive, I found Shopify’s section-based editor a pain to use, since it could hold up the building process. The editor feels restrictive, so I recommend using Shopify’s new AI tool to create custom blocks and designs for you instead.

How Much Does Shopify Cost?
Shopify’s pricing ranges from $29 to $299 per month (billed annually)
Shopify offers a very brief three-day free trial
Get your first three months for just $1 per month when you sign up
Online credit card rates and third-party transaction fees vary depending on your plan – without Shopify Payments, transaction fees start at 2% on the Basic plan

Why Use Shopify in 2026?

With the rollout of AI and social media, the way customers shop has changed dramatically. They don’t just use Google, but instead look at socials, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and other channels.

Shopify’s Agentic Storefronts help businesses adapt for the era of AI search, getting your products to appear in results within these AI-powered conversations. Customers can then purchase directly from ChatGPT, without needing to visit your website – so, if your New Year’s resolution is to adopt a customer-first strategy, Shopify’s seamless collaboration with AI search engines can’t be ignored.

Shopify is suitable for:
Growing online stores that need powerful tools to scale up with
Businesses that require strong shipping features
Businesses with large inventories

Shopify isn't suitable for:
Novice business owners with limited experience
Design-focused users who want creative freedom
Users who want advanced AI tools

#5. GoDaddy: Best Speedy Setup
💰 Starting price: $10.99 per month (billed annually)
🤖 AI website builder: Yes
💻 Read our GoDaddy review for more information

We recommend using GoDaddy, instead of Wix or Shopify, if you’re looking for a simple builder to get your website live quickly.

GoDaddy’s onboarding process is super efficient and can be completed in less than 30 seconds, though it’s not as personalized as Wix’s setup. And, while GoDaddy favors speed and simplicity, its basic features do limit its user base. For this reason, GoDaddy is best suited for personal or informational sites.

✔️ Pros
Fast onboarding
Budget-friendly plans
Editor tutorial for beginners
Social post creator and calendar

❌ Cons
Section-based editor limits creativity
AI templates are dull
Needs clearer SEO advice

GoDaddy has launched Airo Builder to help you build and develop web apps with AI – the vibe coding tool is the latest entry to the market, following Hostinger Horizons, Wix Vibe, and Shopify Sidekick.

When testing GoDaddy, I found myself ticking off essential tasks with no real headache, such as editing my site’s SEO and adding products. However, I did have some difficulty with the backend navigation at points, and I had to spend a fair chunk of time polishing my site’s design (because of GoDaddy’s lackluster options), which sort of counters the user-friendly image. For a builder that positions itself as a good option for beginners, I’d argue GoDaddy needs to improve its user experience to compete with other easy-to-use builders.

How Much Does GoDaddy Cost?
GoDaddy’s pricing ranges from $10.99 to $23.99 per month (billed annually)
You can stay on GoDaddy’s free plan forever, but it has limitations, like ads
You’ll need the $23.99 per month Commerce plan to sell online
GoDaddy charges 2.7% + $0.30 per transaction

Why Use GoDaddy in 2026?

In 2026, businesses need to operate and engage with customers across multiple channels, including social media – it’s not enough to just have a website if you’re looking to build brand awareness. GoDaddy’s AI-driven content tools, campaign automation, and marketing suite (including GoDaddy Airo and GoDaddy Studio) make it quick and easy for your business to build connections online.

GoDaddy is suitable for:
Users who need to create a website quickly
Businesses with a good social media presence
Service-based businesses

GoDaddy isn't suitable for:
Users who want modern, aesthetic design options
Businesses that need to integrate with third-party apps or software

How Do I Choose The Right Website Builder?

To choose the right website builder, you should evaluate eight key factors, ranging from user experience and AI capabilities to scalability and SEO features. While we can help you compare website builders, you have to determine your needs and must-haves, and identify what you can live without.

Below, I’ve put together a checklist of key factors to consider when researching or trialing a website builder:
User experience: Is the builder easy to use and navigate? Is the onboarding process straightforward? Is the editor drag-and-drop?
AI support: Is there an AI website builder? Can you get instant advice from an AI assistant? Can you use AI to create text, images, and product descriptions?
Templates: How many templates and design options are available? Are they free?
Ecommerce features: Does the builder let you sell products or services online? Do you need to pay transaction fees? Can you promote your business?
Pricing: Is the builder good value for money? What features do you get for the price you pay? Can you test things out with a free plan or free trial? Are there additional costs to consider, such as a custom domain name?
SEO: What SEO features are included with the plan you’re looking at? Can you optimize your pages? Does the builder have good loading times? Is it easy to track your site’s performance?
Customer support: Does the builder offer a tutorial? Can you get in contact with the builder’s customer service team 24/7? Are there online resources?
Scalability: Is there room to grow your website or business? Can you connect to other channels, such as social media or online marketplaces?

Watch our video to learn more about each website builder’s benefits and drawbacks:

Can I Switch Website Builders?

All five of our top-rated website builders allow you to cancel your plan and move to another platform. However, switching isn’t straightforward. The difficulty will depend on the builders you’re switching between.

In most cases, you’ll need to start from scratch again. That means redesigning your website, adding your products, and setting up your backend, with your new builder of choice. If you have a custom domain with your existing builder, you can usually swap this to your new provider.

How We Test and Rank Website Builders

This year, we put 12 leading website builders through an in-depth testing process to determine our ranking and recommendations. Our research team has spent over 300 hours analyzing each builder, covering 207 areas of investigation in total.

We’ve focused on six core categories – each category has been given a unique weighting to reflect what our readers value the most:
Website Functionality: 30%

We examine each builder’s site speed and the quality of features available, including SEO and marketing.
Design Features: 25%

We assess each website builder’s AI building tools, aesthetic capabilities, and template options.
Pricing: 15%

We review the pricing of each website builder to see what you get for the money you pay.
User Experience: 15%

We test each builder ourselves to assess its ease of use and accessibility – this helps us speak from experience when recommending a platform.
Help and Support: 10%

We look at a website builder’s support options and responsiveness.
Reputation: 5%

We test how a website builder performs in the wider market to see how it compares to competitors and if users would recommend it.

I also know just what it’s like to use a builder’s editor and features myself, since I carried out hands-on testing with each of the builders we reviewed. You can read my thoughts on this year’s research below:

My Website Builder Testing Summary

After testing each of these builders, I have my personal favorites (looking at you, Squarespace and Hostinger ), but I stand by our rankings and recommendations. And that’s what makes it so important to read through a list like ours – the perfect builder for one user might not be the right fit for another, so it’s worth knowing what your business needs the most and testing out each platform for yourself.

Wix remains our champion because it’s difficult for any other builder to compete with the sheer quality and quantity of features, templates, and customization it offers. I was really impressed by Wix’s editor, particularly its AI chatbot builder, since this simplified the onboarding process for me.

Squarespace and Hostinger are incredibly easy to use, with Squarespace offering stunning templates and Hostinger providing a suite of AI tools to save you time and energy. And, while I found the experience of using Shopify a little underwhelming, its sales features and scalability are ideal for growing stores. GoDaddy, on the other hand, focuses on simplicity and speed, which will lend itself well to beginners and basic websites.

Emma Ryan Lead Writer

Final Verdict: Which Builder Do I Recommend?

Our research process has determined the top five website builders, and Wix is the best builder for website and business management, whether you’re looking to build a blog or start selling online.

Each website builder has its strengths – and weaknesses – so I know Wix won’t be the right fit for everyone. If you’re unsure of where to start, I recommend checking out the available free plans or free trials to figure out what works best for you.

FAQs

As a starting point, you can use a free plan to build your website and set up your future inventory. However, if you’re looking to present your site as a professional storefront down the line, it’s worth upgrading right away to remove ads and add a custom domain name. You’ll need to upgrade eventually to accept payments and sell products, so it makes sense to start with a premium plan immediately.

Alternatively, you can choose a dedicated ecommerce builder, like Shopify, right away and skip the free plan altogether.

Yes, you can switch to another website builder and cancel your existing plan, but the process isn’t easy. Most builders want to lock you into their platform, so migrating to another is a very manual job – there’s no simple button to transfer all of your pages and content over to a new builder.

You’ll need to design your site again, configure your settings, and set up your inventory for selling. That’s why it’s best to do your research beforehand so you find the right website builder for you in the long-term.

Wix is the best website builder for small business thanks to its drag-and-drop editor, built-in features (such as email marketing), and personalized SEO support. You can get started with its free plan, which is great for entrepreneurs on a budget, but you’ll need to upgrade eventually to start selling online. Ecommerce plans start from $29 per month, but you can save 10% with our code TAKE10.

Wix has the best AI tools we’ve tested, including an AI website builder to help you design and generate a custom template based on your website needs. You can also use Wix’s AI Theme Assistant to get design support directly in the drag-and-drop editor.

Other builders, such as Shopify, also provide great AI tools for website design. For example, Shopify recently improved its AI-powered assistant, Shopify Sidekick. Now, you can click on an area of your site you’d like to tweak, and Sidekick will do the design work for you.

Based on our testing, Wix has the best SEO features. Not only does Wix handle the SEO basics, such as mobile optimization, but it also provides you with a personalized SEO checklist based on your website’s immediate needs. And, for SEO beginners, Wix offers an SEO Learning Hub full of guides, videos, and online courses.

WordPress.org is an open-source CMS (Content Management System), not a dedicated website builder, like Wix or Squarespace. You can build and create websites with WordPress.org, but you need to source and manage everything yourself, including hosting, integrations, security, and software updates.

For example, you can connect your WordPress.org site with Shopify to help sell products online – but I’d just recommend using Shopify if your goal is to set up an online store.

There’s also WordPress.com, which behaves more like a traditional website builder. However, it’s more of a blogging platform, and lacks the functionality of builders like Wix.

## How Do I Choose The Right Website Builder?

To choose the right website builder, you should evaluate eight key factors, ranging from user experience and AI capabilities to scalability and SEO features. While we can help you [compare website builders](https://www.websitebuilderexpert.com/website-builders/comparisons/), you have to determine your needs and must-haves, and identify what you can live without.

Below, I’ve put together a checklist of key factors to consider when researching or trialing a website builder:
**User experience:** Is the builder easy to use and navigate? Is the onboarding process straightforward? Is the editor drag-and-drop?
**AI support:** Is there an [AI website builder](https://www.websitebuilderexpert.com/website-builders/best-ai-website-builders/)? Can you get instant advice from an AI assistant? Can you use AI to create text, images, and product descriptions?
**Templates:** How many templates and design options are available? Are they free?
**Ecommerce features:** Does the builder let you sell products or services online? Do you need to pay transaction fees? Can you promote your business?
**Pricing:** Is the builder good value for money? What features do you get for the price you pay? Can you test things out with a free plan or free trial? Are there additional costs to consider, such as a custom domain name?
**SEO:** What SEO features are included with the plan you’re looking at? Can you optimize your pages? Does the builder have good loading times? Is it easy to track your site’s performance?
**Customer support:** Does the builder offer a tutorial? Can you get in contact with the builder’s customer service team 24/7? Are there online resources?
**Scalability:** Is there room to grow your website or business? Can you connect to other channels, such as social media or online marketplaces?

### Can I Switch Website Builders?

All five of our top-rated website builders allow you to cancel your plan and move to another platform. However, **switching isn’t straightforward**. The difficulty will depend on the builders you’re switching between.

As a starting point, you can use a free plan to build your website and set up your future inventory. However, if you’re looking to present your site as a professional storefront down the line, it’s worth upgrading right away to remove ads and add a custom domain name. You’ll need to upgrade eventually to accept payments and sell products, so it makes sense to start with a premium plan immediately.

Alternatively, you can choose a dedicated **ecommerce** builder, like **Shopify**, right away and skip the free plan altogether.

Yes, you can switch to another website builder and cancel your existing plan, but the process isn’t easy. Most builders want to lock you into their platform, so migrating to another is a very manual job – there’s no simple button to transfer all of your pages and content over to a new builder.

You’ll need to design your site again, configure your settings, and set up your inventory for selling. That’s why it’s best to do your research beforehand so you find the right website builder for you in the long-term.
